title: Analytics
description: Track views and engagement metrics for your shared LiveFolio folios.
content: Analytics Overview LiveFolio tracks engagement metrics for shared folios: - How many people viewed your folio - When views occurred - Which slides got the most attention (deck mode) - Reaction counts View Tracking Each time someone opens a share URL, LiveFolio records: - Timestamp — when the view occurred - Referrer — where the viewer came from (if available) - Anonymous — no personal data collected from public viewers For organization-restricted folios, admins can see viewer-level data. Reaction Counts Aggregate emoji reaction counts per version: Comment Activity Track open vs. resolved comments to gauge feedback activity. Available in the dashboard and via API. Accessing Analytics Dashboard Per-folio view counts, comment counts, and last-updated timestamps. API Requires authentication. Returns view events and engagement data. Via MCP The tool returns per-project summaries including count. Interpreting Analytics - High views, low reactions — reaching people but not engaging them - Many comments on a slide — that section needs attention - Steady growth — being shared organically - Sudden spike — likely shared on social media Privacy - Public folios: views tracked anonymously, no personal identifiers - Organization-restricted: admins see viewer-level data - No third-party tracking services used

title: Billing & Invoices
description: Plans, upgrading, invoices, and managing your subscription on LiveFolio Cloud. Billing is Cloud-only — a self-hosted instance has none.
content: Plans Plan Price Notes --- --- --- Free $0 Get started, publish, and share folios Pro $8 / month Single seat Team $15 / seat / month Per-seat, message allowances pool across the workspace Enterprise Custom Volume pricing with a 10-seat minimum — contact us for SSO, audit, and dedicated infrastructure AI is never the meter. Message allowances exist to keep costs predictable — but connecting your own agent (Claude, GPT, Cursor, any MCP client) publishes unlimited folios on every plan , including Free. Self-hosting? There is no billing in LiveFolio OSS. No plans, no limits, no invoices — see Self-Hosting. Upgrading Settings → Billing shows your current plan, this month's usage, and the upgrade options. Choosing a plan opens a Stripe Checkout page where you enter payment details. - Team — pick your seat count before checkout; the slider sets it. - Enterprise — contact us; we'll set up your workspace. Your plan takes effect as soon as the payment completes. The workspace is upgraded by a webhook, not by the browser redirect, so it can take a moment — refreshing the page is enough. Invoices Every billing cycle produces an invoice, and they're listed in Settings → Billing → Invoices with the date, amount, and status. Click any row to open Stripe's hosted invoice, where you can view, download a PDF, or pay an outstanding balance. Renewals are billed automatically, so the list doubles as your payment history. Managing your subscription Manage Subscription opens the Stripe Billing Portal, where you can: - Update the payment method on file - Change seats (Team) - Cancel or resume the subscription - Download past invoices and receipts Use the Portal rather than asking us to change something by hand — it's immediate and keeps your billing record consistent. If a payment fails Stripe retries failed charges automatically (smart dunning), and your plan stays active while it retries — an expired card shouldn't cost you access. While a retry is pending, Settings → Billing shows a not

title: Comments & Feedback
description: Leave canvas annotations, emoji reactions, and manage feedback on shared LiveFolio folios.
content: Canvas Annotations Canvas annotations are comments pinned to a specific position on a folio. Reviewers click anywhere on a shared folio to leave context-rich feedback. Annotation Data Each annotation includes: Managing Comments As the folio owner, you can: - View all comments in the editor — organized by slide/page and position - Resolve comments — mark as addressed without deleting - Reply — the editor chat panel supports threaded discussions - Delete — remove outdated or irrelevant feedback Emoji Reactions Viewers can leave quick emoji reactions on shared folios: - 👍 Like - 🎉 Celebrate - 🚀 Mind-blowing - ❤️ Love - 👀 Seen Reactions are tracked per-version and displayed as aggregate counts. Reactions API The Curated Brief In the editor, the AI assistant can generate a curated design brief from open comments. This brief: 1. Collects all unresolved annotations 2. Organizes them by slide/page and position 3. Provides context (target element, selector, suggested fix) 4. Formats everything as a structured design document This is also available via MCP with the tool — AI agents can read the brief to understand what changes reviewers want. Example Brief Snippet Feedback Workflow 1. Publish a folio and share the URL 2. Reviewers leave annotations and reactions 3. Review feedback in the editor 4. Use the curated brief to understand what needs changing 5. Edit and re-publish — new version incorporates feedback 6. Resolve comments once addressed Best Practices - Encourage specific annotations — "change the header color to blue" is better than "looks wrong" - Resolve, don't delete — resolved comments create an audit trail - Check the brief before editing — the AI-generated summary saves time - Use reactions for quick sentiment — not every review needs a written comment

title: FAQ
description: Frequently asked questions about LiveFolio — folios, sharing, MCP, integrations, and troubleshooting.
content: General What is LiveFolio? LiveFolio is a publishing platform for interactive HTML documents. It replaces PDFs and slide decks with living, shareable web pages that support versioning, comments, and reactions. How do I get started? Sign up at your LiveFolio instance, then create your first folio. Folios What can a folio include? HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and binary assets (images, fonts) encoded as base64 Data URLs. Is there a size limit? Check your instance's plan for specific limits. Typical limits range from 5 MB to 25 MB per folio. Can I edit after publishing? Yes. Every edit creates a new version. Published versions are immutable — previous work is always recoverable. Sharing Who can see my shared folio? Anyone with the share URL. You can restrict access to your organization, add password protection, or set expiring links. How do I stop sharing? Set the folio to private in dashboard settings, or via the API. Can I embed a folio? Yes. Use an pointing to the share URL. MCP & AI Agents Can my AI agent publish folios? Yes. Connect your agent via MCP — see Integrations. Your agent can create, update, and manage folios from your editor. How do I set it up? Go to Settings → API Keys , generate a key, and add the MCP config to your agent. Takes under a minute. What agents are supported? Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI — any MCP-compatible agent. Integrations Can I get notifications in Slack? Yes. Connect Slack from Connections ( ). You'll get notified about new comments, versions, and shares. What about Discord? Same capabilities. Connect your Discord server from the Connections page. Troubleshooting Folio won't publish Check that your HTML is valid and you have publish permissions in your workspace. Share link doesn't work Verify the folio is set to public and hasn't been deleted. Check access control settings. Agent can't connect 1. Verify the API key is valid (not revoked) 2. Check the MCP URL is correct 3. Ensure the header is properly formatted

You can: - Write or paste HTML, CSS, and JavaScript - Preview in real-time - Choose a project mode - Apply design system themes, palettes, and typography Project Modes Mode Use Case Layout --- --- --- Document Articles, reports, guides Vertical scroll with sidebar Deck Presentations, slide decks Horizontal panels + keyboard nav Spreadsheet Tables, calculators Grid with formula support Dashboard Metrics, KPIs, charts Card-based with visualizations Publish Click "Publish" to save your folio. Each publish: - Creates a new immutable version - Generates a shareable URL - Makes the folio available for feedback You can continue editing — changes won't affect the published version until you publish again. The Editor The editor ( ) is where you build folios: - HTML editor with live preview - Project mode selector — document, deck, spreadsheet, dashboard - Design system picker — theme, palette, typography - Reference files — upload documents for AI context - Chat panel — ask the AI assistant to modify your folio Connect Your AI Agent LiveFolio is built for AI agents. title: User Guide
description: Create, share, version, and collect feedback on interactive HTML documents with LiveFolio.
content: Welcome LiveFolio turns HTML documents into interactive, versioned folios — shareable web pages with built-in feedback and analytics. This guide covers the LiveFolio platform: - Getting Started — Create your first folio - Sharing — Publish and share via public URLs - Version Control — History, compare, restore - Comments & Feedback — Annotations and reactions - Analytics — Views and engagement - Design Systems — Themes, palettes, typography - Integrations — Connect AI agents, Slack, Discord - FAQ — Common questions How LiveFolio Works 1. Create a folio in the editor — write HTML, CSS, JS, or have an AI agent generate it 2. Publish to get a shareable URL — anyone with the link can view it 3. Collect feedback — viewers leave canvas annotations and emoji reactions 4. Iterate — every publish creates an immutable version; restore any previous state Core Concepts Folios An interactive HTML document. It can include JavaScript, CSS, and embedded assets. Each folio has a unique ID, version history, and a shareable URL. Versions Every publish creates an immutable version. Browse history, compare changes, and restore any previous state. Versions never change once published. Sharing Publish a folio to get a public URL. Share it with anyone. Control access with organization-only visibility, password protection, and expiring links. Feedback Reviewers leave canvas annotations (comments pinned to specific positions on the folio) and emoji reactions . All feedback is tied to the current version. Integrations Connect AI coding agents via MCP to publish folios directly from your editor. Link Slack and Discord for real-time notifications. See Integrations.

title: Sharing a Folio
description: Publish your interactive folios and share them via public URLs, with access control and embedding support.
content: Publishing When you publish a folio from the editor, it becomes available at a shareable URL. The share page renders your folio fullscreen with a minimal toolbar for comments and reactions. Anyone with the link can view the folio. No account is required to view a shared folio. Access Control Control who can see your folios: - Public — anyone with the link - Organization-only — restricted to members of your workspace - Password-protected — viewers enter a passphrase to access - Expiring links — links stop working after a set date Configure these from the folio settings in the dashboard or via the API. Making a Folio Public Via API: Via MCP: Embedding Embed any folio in an external webpage: The embedded folio is fully interactive and respects sharing permissions. Comments and Reactions on Shared Folios Viewers can interact with shared folios without an account: - Canvas comments — click anywhere on the folio to leave pinned feedback - Emoji reactions — quick 👍, 🎉, 🚀, ❤️ responses - Analytics — view counts are tracked automatically Stopping Sharing To stop sharing a folio, set it to private: The share URL immediately stops working. title: Version Control
description: Browse version history, compare changes between versions, and roll back to any previous state of your folio.
content: How Versioning Works Every time you publish a folio, a new immutable version is created. LiveFolio's versioning system is designed to be simple and safe: - Immutable versions — once published, a version never changes - Incremental numbering — versions are labeled , , , etc. - Full file snapshots — each version stores the complete state of all files - Commit messages — each version has a description of what changed Version History Each folio maintains a complete version history. You can view it: - In the editor — version timeline sidebar - Via the API — returns the full version array - Via MCP — returns with IDs, messages, and file lists Version Data Structure Restoring a Previous Version To restore a previous version: 1. Open the folio in the editor 2. Browse version history to find the version you want 3. Click "Restore" — this creates a new version with the old content 4. The restored version gets a new version ID (e.g., ) with a note like "Restored from v2" Restoration never overwrites history — it always creates a new version. Your complete history is preserved. File Merging When updating a folio (via MCP or API), files are merged with the latest version: - Files you specify in overwrite or add to the existing set - Files you don't mention remain unchanged from the previous version - This means you only need to send the files that changed This merge behavior is key for efficient AI agent workflows — an agent can update just the CSS without re-sending the entire HTML file. Best Practices - Write descriptive commit messages — future you will thank you - Publish often — small, frequent versions are easier to review - Use version history as an undo stack — if an edit goes wrong, restore the previous version - Review before sharing — always check the latest version before sharing with others

title: MCP Authentication
description: How authentication works — API keys, auth.md agent registration, and connecting agents to LiveFolio.
content: Getting an API Key 1. Go to Settings → API Keys in the dashboard 2. Click Generate Agent Key 3. Give it a name (e.g., "Claude Code", "Cursor") 4. Copy the key — it's shown only once The key format: Using Your Key Include the key as a Bearer token in the header. The endpoint is Streamable HTTP — use in modern clients: If your MCP client doesn't support custom headers, pass the key as a query parameter: Cold requests without valid credentials get an HTTP 401 with a header pointing at — agents can self-discover the registration flow from that challenge. How Auth Works Agent-Native Registration (auth.md) LiveFolio implements the open auth.md protocol. Agents can autonomously register and acquire API keys — no human dashboard interaction needed. Discovery Agents discover auth endpoints from the protected resource metadata: User Claimed Flow (OTP) 1. Register — initialize an anonymous session: 2. Claim — send the user's email to trigger a 6-digit code: 3. Complete — user provides the code, session upgrades to persistent API key: The full protocol guide is served at : Key Management - Name keys descriptively — "Claude Code (MacBook)" not "key1" - One key per agent — don't share keys between tools - Rotate regularly — generate new keys and revoke old ones - Revoke instantly — delete a key from Settings to invalidate all connections using it Troubleshooting "Unauthorized" error 1. Verify the key hasn't been revoked (check Settings → API Keys) 2. Check the header format: 3. Ensure the key belongs to the correct workspace Agent can't discover auth endpoints The and endpoints are public. If they're not reachable, check your instance URL. Self-Hosted Auth Self-hosted instances have different authentication behavior. See Self-Hosting: Configuration for details.

title: MCP Troubleshooting
description: Common MCP errors and how to fix them — connection issues, auth failures, and tool-specific problems.
content: Connection Issues "Connection refused" or "Streamable HTTP connection failed" Check: - Your instance URL is correct - The MCP endpoint is (include the full path) - Your client transport matches the server: use (Streamable HTTP POST) in modern clients — the legacy SSE GET transport exists for older clients - Your network can reach the instance (try ) Agent shows no tools available The MCP handshake didn't complete. Most clients handle this automatically. If using a custom client: 1. Call with 2. Wait for response 3. Call 4. Then call Authentication Errors "Unauthorized" or 401 1. Verify the API key is valid (not expired or revoked) — check Settings → API Keys 2. Check the header format: 3. If using query parameter: 4. Key belongs to the correct workspace 5. If you're mid-registration: the token is a polling credential only — it 401s on . Wait for the key instead. Key was working but stopped Someone may have revoked it. Generate a new key from Settings → API Keys. Tool Errors "Project not found" - Call first to get valid project IDs - IDs are case-sensitive - Verify the project belongs to your workspace "Argument is required" Check the Tools Reference for required parameters. "Error executing tool" Check the server logs for details. Common causes: - Invalid HTML in or - File size exceeding limits - Database write failure Debugging Test with curl Inspect Project State If a tool returns unexpected results, call to inspect the full project state — all files, versions, and comments. Self-Hosted Troubleshooting For tunnel issues, database problems, and OSS-specific MCP errors, see Self-Hosting.

title: Analytics
description: View tracking and engagement metrics — page views, session time, and device breakdowns.
content: Overview The analytics endpoint tracks page views and engagement time for shared folios. It is designed as a lightweight beacon — no authentication is required, and the endpoint is resilient to empty or malformed bodies. Analytics data includes: - Views — total unique page loads - Total time — cumulative seconds viewers have spent on the folio - Average time — average seconds per view - Device breakdown — mobile vs desktop view counts Track Analytics Sends an analytics beacon for a folio view. The client should call this endpoint: 1. On initial page load — with to increment the view counter 2. Periodically during the session — to accumulate session time (e.g., every 30 seconds) Request Body: Field Type Required Description --- --- --- --- number No Seconds to add to total time (default: 0) boolean No Whether this is the first beacon for this view (increments view count) string No or other (defaults to desktop) Example — Initial page load beacon: Example — Periodic time tracking beacon: Response: Note: An empty body is handled gracefully and returns success without error. Example Request: Response (relevant field): Update Reactions Sets (replaces) reaction counts. The provided counts are merged with existing counts — you can update one emoji without affecting others. Counts must be non-negative integers. Validation Rules - Only the four supported emojis are accepted: 👍, ❤️, 💡, 🔥 - Counts must be non-negative numbers (negative values are ignored) - Non-integer counts are floored to integers - Unknown emoji keys are silently dropped - Each update merges with existing counts (not a full replace of all emojis)

title: Uploading Files
description: Upload single files or batch upload images to a folio via the REST API.
content: Overview LiveFolio provides two endpoints for uploading files into an existing folio's latest version. These are designed for programmatic asset uploads from CI/CD pipelines, design tools, or build scripts. Use the PUT /api/files/{id} endpoint for full versioned updates. Use upload endpoints when you only need to add or overwrite individual files. Single File Upload Uploads a single file as raw binary data. The file path is specified via the header. Headers: Header Required Description --- --- --- Yes Bearer API key Yes Must be Yes Target path within the folio (e.g., , ) Body: Raw binary file content. Limits: - Maximum file size: 25 MB - Supported image formats: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, ICO, SVG, BMP Example Request: Response: Error Responses: Status Error Description --- --- --- 400 No file path specified 404 Folio does not exist 413 File exceeds 25 MB limit Batch Upload (Multipart) Uploads multiple files in a single request using . All files are applied to the folio's latest version in one transaction. This endpoint bypasses Next.js body size limits because multipart data is streamed, not buffered. It also avoids the 33% size overhead of base64 encoding. Request Body: Standard with each part being a file. The part's field is used as the folio file path. Limits: - No hard file count limit (bounded by request timeout) - Supported formats: same as single upload Example Request: Response: Error Responses: Status Error Description --- --- --- 400 No valid files in the request 404 Folio does not exist How It Works Both endpoints write files into the current latest version of the folio. They do not create a new version — the files are merged into the existing file map of the most recent version. For versioned updates (creating a new version with a commit message), use with the and fields. In Cloud mode, uploaded images are automatically processed: base64-encoded images are extracted and stored in the asset store, with the folio version receiving lightweight pointers instead

title: Configuration

content: You probably need to configure nothing A self-hosted LiveFolio runs with no file, no database, and no account . The defaults are correct for local use out of the box. There are two things you may want to change: which AI model you use , and where your data lives . --- AI providers You can supply keys two ways. They're independent — use whichever suits you. In the app (recommended) Open Settings → General and paste keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or DeepSeek, or point at a local Ollama . Keys entered this way are stored in your browser's localStorage and sent only to your own local server with each chat request. They are never written to disk on the server and never leave your machine beyond the provider call itself. Your chat's model menu picks them up immediately. Via environment variables Server-side keys work too, and act as a fallback when no browser key is set — handy for a shared machine or a server you start once: Ollama needs no key at all — it runs on your machine. title: Database
description: How the flat-file JSON database works in self-hosted LiveFolio — structure, locking, backups, and migration.
content: Flat-File Architecture Self-hosted LiveFolio stores all data in a single file: at the project root. No database server is required. Structure File Locking Concurrent writes are protected by file-based advisory locking. When a write is in progress: 1. A file is created 2. Other write attempts wait for the lock to release 3. The lock releases automatically when the write completes This prevents data corruption from concurrent CLI sync and dashboard edits. Performance The flat-file approach is suitable for: - Up to 100 folios (single JSON parse is fast) - Up to 50 versions per folio (file stays under 10 MB) - Single user access (no concurrent read/write contention) For larger workloads, consider migrating to a hosted database. Backups Manual Automated Add to cron: What to Back Up - — all folio data (the one that matters) - — MCP master key and tunnel config That's the whole state. Provider keys live in your browser (or an optional you created yourself), and the app itself is replaceable. Migration To move your folios out of a self-hosted instance: 1. Stop the server 2. Copy the database: 3. Import it wherever you're going, using that target's import path 4. Verify your folios appear there 5. Archive the original There is no proprietary export format — is plain JSON, so your folios are readable with or without LiveFolio. Disaster Recovery If is corrupted: Prevention: - Don't manually edit while the server is running - Use the API or MCP for all data modifications - Keep regular automated backups

title: Self-Hosting Guide

content: Overview LiveFolio is open-source software. You can run it on your own machine with full control over your data, configuration, and infrastructure. There is no to create — provider keys can live in the app UI, and everything else has a working default. Key Characteristics - Local-first — all data stored in a flat file - No login required — single local user - Works offline — no internet needed (except for tunnel sharing and AI providers) - Full MCP support — AI agents publish folios via the MCP server - Unlimited usage — no rate limits, no usage caps - Your API keys — bring your own provider keys, or run Ollama locally - Zero telemetry — nothing phones home Quick Reference Command What it does --- --- Install and run — no clone needed Dev server on port 3001 Production build (pinned to OSS mode) Serve the production build on port 3000 Run the test suite Data Ownership Your data stays on your machine. The flat-file contains all your folios, versions, comments, and settings. Back it up with . No data leaves your machine unless you explicitly share folios via the public tunnel.
